key_insight: Better reliability diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening or reduce DFT verification costs at a required recall.
engineering_relevance: Choose reliability interventions by the DFT effort they save while retaining near-hull candidates, not by diagnostic accuracy alone.
method: Evaluate novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits.
Measure DFT avoided while maintaining required recall of near-hull candidates.
Use two-oracle analysis to distinguish misaligned reliability targets from finite-budget audit limitations.
evidence_signal: Across MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3, successful diagnostics did not reliably improve screening; oracle results differed between formation-energy and hull-aligned screening.
watch_item: Even a decision-aligned reliability target may not yield useful model routing when audit budgets are limited.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
